title: PCA Without the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
subtitle: A variational route through the spectral theorem, SVD, and low-rank approximation
summary: A route to PCA that starts with geometry: compactness and Lagrange multipliers lead to the real spectral theorem, SVD, and optimal low-rank approximation.
prerequisites: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and basic proof techniques.

title: Gradient Descent: What Converges, and How Fast?
subtitle: Stationarity, convex rates, and stochastic gradients
summary: What can gradient descent guarantee, and what changes when gradients are noisy? Proofs trace how smoothness and convexity determine convergence and its speed.
prerequisites: Multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and basic probability.

title: Spectral Clustering Through Courant–Fischer
subtitle: From Lloyd’s algorithm to graph Laplacians and random walks
summary: Why do eigenvectors help reveal clusters? An optimization view connects k-means to spectral clustering, with Courant–Fischer and random walks explaining the construction.
prerequisites: Linear algebra, eigenvalues, and basic optimization.

title: Ridge Regression and the Influence of a Single Point
subtitle: Lagrange multipliers, Cook’s distance, and Sherman–Morrison
summary: How much can one observation change a regression fit? A geometric treatment of ridge regression leads to Cook’s distance through the Sherman–Morrison formula.
prerequisites: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and introductory statistics.

title: Reinforcement Learning I
subtitle: Optimal policies, Bellman operators, and dynamic programming
summary: Why does an optimal policy exist, and how can we find it? A fixed-point argument for finite discounted Markov decision processes leads to value iteration and policy iteration.
prerequisites: Basic probability, linear algebra, and familiarity with metric spaces.

title: From Martingales to Diffusion Generators
subtitle: Itô calculus, scale functions, and exit problems
summary: How can we describe when and where a diffusion leaves a region? Starting with conditional expectation and Itô calculus, these notes connect stochastic paths to boundary-value problems.

title: Black–Scholes Through Replication
subtitle: Risk-neutral pricing, delta, and American exercise
summary: How can a trading strategy determine an option’s price? Replication and risk-neutral valuation lead to Black–Scholes, followed by delta hedging and the question of early exercise.
prerequisites: Brownian motion, Itô’s formula, and basic martingales.
